Turn the Rings Rules

Turn the rings until every ray shows one shape.

The rules

The rings
Three to five rings lie one inside the other, numbered from the inside out. Each ring has 8 fields, each with a shape: circle, ring, triangle, square, star, diamond, cross or crescent moon. Filled and open shapes can be told apart without colour.
Turning
Under the picture every ring has two buttons: ↺ turns it one field to the left (anticlockwise), ↻ one field to the right (clockwise). The ring jumps to its new place at once.
Goal
Dashed lines divide the picture into 8 rays from the middle outwards. The puzzle is solved when each ray shows the same shape on every ring. Different rays may show different shapes.
Coupled rings
On Hard the rings are coupled: turning a ring also turns the next ring outwards by one field in the same direction. The outermost ring turns alone.
Levels
Easy: 3 rings with 4 kinds of shape, 3 to 5 moves. Medium: 4 rings with 6 kinds, 5 to 8 moves. Hard: 5 coupled rings with 8 kinds, 7 to 11 moves. The computer works out the fewest moves for every puzzle; they are shown from the start.
Hint
Hint frames the button of a turn that brings you one step nearer to the solution. Undo takes back the last turn; it counts as a move.

Example

Ring 2 is one field ahead of ring 1. One turn of ring 2 to the left puts the same shape on every ray.
